Answer: D
Reason: The imaging series demonstrates a progression from initial bilateral opacities (Figure 1) to severe diffuse consolidations (Figure 4), followed by complete resolution in the follow-up images (Figures 5a/5b); this rapid onset and full clearance pattern is characteristic of Weil Syndrome (Leptospirosis) or similar acute reversible pneumonitis, distinguishing it from conditions like Goodpasture syndrome which typically leave residual fibrosis. *(guided by t000006)*
